objectClass.notes: Static monumental landmark building, exterior shell only. No interior geometry: a prop kit is only ever looked at from outside, so an interior costs draw calls, geometries and VRAM for something nobody sees. Nothing moves, so one root pivot and zero sockets is the correct contract. The Din Daeng / National Housing Authority single-loaded slab flat: six identical open-corridor floors on +Z between two breeze-block-screened stair towers that stand proud of the corridor line, a dog-leg stair seen through a full-height slot in each tower's end wall, a low gable of corrugated cement sheet inside a parapet over the rear 7.7 m of the depth with the tower tops flat below it, and a plain rear elevation carrying a grid of small louvre windows.

reasoning: The silhouette is a long slab with two solid end towers standing 2.8 m proud of a recessed open corridor and a low gable roof inside a parapet -- three events (tower step, corridor recess, gable) that every three-quarter view shows and a plain box would lose.

The identity is in the REPEATED corridor floor: six identical rows of ochre spandrel over a shaded opening with a door and a louvre window per bay, which the plate shows on one elevation and the registry notes say must be instanced per bay per floor.

Four surfaces carry the rest of the identity -- faded stained ochre, streaked concrete, breeze-block screens, corrugated cement sheet -- and each is a post-construction canvas on a textureless material rather than geometry.
Action readiness is minimal: static exterior shell, box collider, not breakable.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Forty-two doors, one hundred and twenty-six windows, twelve screens, thirty stair parts and six small details are two hundred and sixteen discrete parts; without instancing they are two hundred submissions against a ceiling of 24. Seven InstancedMesh systems carry all of them at one submission each, beside three merged components.

coordinateFrame.notes: Origin base-center as the asset declares, +Y up, the open corridor on +Z. Towers occupy the outer 3.3 m of each end at full depth; the spandrel line sits at z = +2.45, the corridor back wall at z = +0.95, the tower fronts at z = +5.25. silhouette.description: A 26.5 x 10.5 m slab from a 0.2 m plinth: towers to 16.0 m, the roof parapet to 16.7 m, the gable-end parapets to 17.5 m over a corrugated sheet whose eaves sit at 16.35 and ridge at 17.3. Six corridor rows at a 2.633 m pitch -- 0.98 m of spandrel plus coping over a 1.5 m opening -- recessed 2.8 m behind the tower fronts across the 19.9 m between them. The silhouette events are the tower step at each end, the corridor recess, the flat tower tops below the gable, and the stair slot on each end face.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: Height is the primary axis at the declared 17.50 m: the gable-end parapet ridge. The Meshy v7 proxy of the plate normalises to w:h:d = 1.514 : 1 : 0.597, so w = 17.5 x 1.514 = 26.5 and d = 17.5 x 0.597 = 10.4 -> 10.50. The plate agrees: its +X end face and its front face foreshorten almost equally at the ~45-degree three-quarter (237 px of depth against 615 px of width). The list-time 28 x 12 was an eight-bay estimate and was corrected on the asset before the build, with the arithmetic in its notes. x spans -13.35..+13.35 (walls at 13.25 plus the 0.10 m plinth step), z spans -5.35..+5.35 the same way, y 0.00..17.50.
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: Independent Meshy v7 reconstruction of the same plate normalises to w:h:d = 1.514 : 1 : 0.597 against the corrected declaration 1.514 : 1 : 0.600. Area-weighted band comparison against the built candidate gives mean |delta width| 0.025 and |delta depth| 0.030 of height across ten bands, the largest single residuals being band 0 (the plinth step, +0.051 depth) and band 9 (the roof, -0.039 width, where the proxy fuses the gable parapets into a wider cap). The proxy DROPPED a corridor row -- it shows five slab bands at a 0.18 H pitch where the plate shows six spandrel rows at 73 px -- so the row count is taken from the plate and the tower width, the spandrel recess and the roof profile from the proxy's +Z and +X depth maps.

featureReviews.evidence: Six corridor rows at a 2.633 m pitch from the 0.2 m plinth, ground floor included, each a 0.98 m ochre spandrel with a concrete coping over a 1.5 m opening onto a back wall 1.5 m behind the spandrel line and 2.8 m behind the tower fronts; a door left and a louvre window right of every one of seven bays; mould along the coping line and rust runs on every spandrel, shifted per floor. Band table against the proxy: mean |delta width| 0.025 of height.
featureReviews.notes: Row count from the plate's six spandrel rows (the proxy dropped one, exactly as the apartment proxy did); the tower width (10/80 of the proxy width), the spandrel recess (0.13 H behind the tower front on the +Z depth map) and the tower inner side face visible on the plate (65 px against a 60 px front at equal foreshortening) agree on the 2.8 m step. The back wall's 0.40 linear tint is the plate's own 0.66 sRGB ratio of shaded wall to lit spandrel, and the recess renders at luma 104 front-on. The first build's grime was 90 hard blotches per strip and read as leopard spots; it is now a continuous mould gradient with 34 soft elliptical clouds and 22 rust streaks.

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the hero4x class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

drawCalls.note: Three components and seven repetition systems: 10 of 24. Everything concrete is one draw, everything ochre one draw, and the 216 repeated parts ride seven InstancedMesh systems.

materials.note: Nine of sixteen. concrete covers the shell entire; ochre the spandrels and back wall with a vertex tint; stair is a gate-driven separate paint for the flights and landings; foliage and cloth are tinted bases for the two small detail systems.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 3,256 of 32,000. The shell is thirty-three boxes and two extrusions, the corridor seven boxes; every instanced part is a single box. A slab block earns its identity from surfaces, not tessellation, and the headroom is deliberate for a prop a level builder places by the dozen.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: Axis-aligned boxes for the shell, corridor, doors, windows, screens and stair parts; two extrusions in the YZ plane for the gable-end parapets and one for the roof prism. The stair slot is a cavity bounded by the tower's own boxes, not a subtraction, so the shell has no interior coincidence.
Seven InstancedMesh systems carry 216 of the prop's 219 discrete parts: 42 doors, 126 windows, 12 screens, 20 flights, 10 landings, 4 plants and 2 laundry racks.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.

Every material is declared textureless. Five post-construction canvases are assigned in the browser only -- concrete streaks and grooves, spandrel grime and rust, roof corrugation, louvre slats and breeze slots -- all seeded, all drawn in multiplier space over white so the authored albedo stays the mean; none is the five-canvas procedural set. Under Node every material renders flat at its authored colour.
